about: The RANGE: a dormant Active Directory practice lab for OSCP-style training. SecuRAX does not reinvent it: it wraps GOAD (Orange Cyberdefense, upstream, pinned to a commit) with the same lifecycle verbs as everything else — wake, hibernate (VMs stop, disks kept), snapshot, prune. Nothing exists until you install it, and it never runs by accident.

MINILAB.what: 1 forest, 1 domain: a DC (Server 2019) + a Windows 10 workstation. The first lab to learn on.

GOAD-Light.what: 1 forest, 2 domains. Smaller GOAD for a smaller PC.

SCCM.what: 1 domain with Microsoft Configuration Manager installed.

GOAD.what: The full lab: 2 forests, 3 domains, 5 VMs. The closest thing to an OSCP AD set.

source_of_numbers: Sum of cpus/mem in each lab's providers/virtualbox/Vagrantfile at the pinned commit. Other providers can differ; disk use is large (tens of GB per lab): check GOAD's docs before you install.

virtualbox.note: Free. Needs VirtualBox + Vagrant on the host. Not available inside WSL2/Docker.

proxmox.note: The right home for it: a dedicated machine (your future burrow). Needs Proxmox + Terraform + Ansible.

ludus.note: Purpose-built cyber-range manager on Proxmox; GOAD has a Ludus environment guide.

aws.note: Ephemeral lab in your AWS account. Costs real money while it exists; a vulnerable AD must be isolated.

warnings: GOAD is deliberately vulnerable: run it ONLY on an isolated host-only/lab network, never on a network with real data or a route to the internet-facing estate.
It uses free Windows evaluation images (180 days). After that, rebuild the lab (an install takes hours and downloads many GB).
OSCP exam rules: use SecuRAX for study; OffSec restricts AI assistance during the exam. Verify the current rules yourself.
